consistencyRules.message: No visible pathology was selected, but other findings are present. Check the inputs.

commonErrors: Ignoring the order of precedence (evacuated, then mass lesion, then shift, then cisterns).
Using a later scan without stating it.
name: Marshall CT Classification

version.label: Marshall CT classification (1991)
version.detail: Six categories: diffuse injury I–IV, evacuated mass lesion (V), non-evacuated mass lesion >25 mL (VI). Category is derived here from the findings in the published order of precedence.

purpose: CT classification of traumatic brain injury.
intendedPopulation: Patients with traumatic brain injury, typically moderate to severe.

inputDefinitions.label: High- or mixed-density lesion >25 mL (not evacuated)

resultStates.label: Diffuse injury I
resultStates.summary: No visible intracranial pathology on this CT at this assessment.
resultStates.detail: A normal CT does not exclude diffuse axonal injury.

resultStates.label: Diffuse injury II
resultStates.summary: Cisterns present, shift 0–5 mm, no lesion >25 mL.

resultStates.label: Diffuse injury III (swelling)
resultStates.summary: Cisterns compressed or absent, shift 0–5 mm, no lesion >25 mL.

resultStates.label: Diffuse injury IV (shift)
resultStates.summary: Midline shift >5 mm, no lesion >25 mL.
resultStates.detail: Correlate with clinical status according to local protocol.

resultStates.label: Evacuated mass lesion (V)
resultStates.detail: Category reflects surgical management; correlate with clinical status.

resultStates.label: Non-evacuated mass lesion (VI)
resultStates.summary: High- or mixed-density lesion >25 mL, not evacuated.
resultStates.detail: Correlate with clinical status according to local protocol.

clinicalContext.text: A widely used CT classification in TBI research and prognostic models.

clinicalInsights.text: The Rotterdam score adds epidural mass and IVH/tSAH and may discriminate better.

limitations.text: Category V depends on whether surgery was done, not only on imaging.

confounders.effect: Lesions evolve after the first scan.

guideSections.what: A six-category CT classification of TBI.
guideSections.whenToUse: Admission CT in TBI, for description and research.
guideSections.howToPerform: Record the findings; the category is derived in the standard order of precedence.
guideSections.clinicalContext: A descriptor and prognostic model input.

sources.citation: Marshall LF, Marshall SB, Klauber MR, et al. A new classification of head injury based on computerized tomography. J Neurosurg. 1991;75(Suppl):S14-S20.

components.label: High- or mixed-density lesion >25 mL (not evacuated)
